# Atlas Tasker

> The ticketing system for you and your AI agents: terminal tickets, Atlas Home, and MCP tools, all in one binary.

Atlas Tasker is a free, MIT-licensed, local-first issue tracker for macOS and Linux. Tickets are Markdown files in your repository, every change is an audited event, and humans and coding agents share queues, dependencies, runs, evidence, gates, and handoffs. Ordinary onboarding is `tracker init` then `tracker`. Lightweight by design: no hosted account. The Home service is a local loopback process, not a cloud daemon. v1.17 adds chat-native boards and security hardening.

The one-line installer selects the latest published GitHub release (v1.17.0). It needs curl, tar, and GitHub CLI (gh) for local attestation-bundle verification without GitHub login. `go install ...@latest` builds the latest tagged module from source and reports `version: "dev"` without release build stamps. Ordinary onboarding is `tracker init` then `tracker`. See verification results on the GitHub release page.

Install the published binary with `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myrrazor/atlas-tasker/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`.

## Guidance for agents
Use this file as a site index, not a full-site corpus. To operate Atlas Tasker on a user's machine, prefer the CLI with `--json` and run `tracker --help` for the current command set; exit codes 0-7 and `error.code` values are stable. `mkdir app && cd app` then `tracker init` then `tracker` is ordinary onboarding so the default project key is `APP`; user-scoped MCP is named `atlas-tasker` and runs `tracker mcp serve --global --tool-profile workflow`, and cross-workspace writes need `workspace_id`. Restart the coding agent after init. Grok also needs project trust before local skills appear. A written config is not a live connection. Ordinary init does not open the integration picker; that is `tracker init --integrations`. Pinned `--workspace` serve is still supported and also defaults to `--tool-profile workflow`; pass `--tool-profile read` or `--read-only` for inspection. Grok registrations add `--tool-name-style portable`. Codex skills write `.agents/skills/atlas-worker/` (`.codex/skills` still lists on 0.144.5). Grok skills write `.grok/skills/atlas-worker/`. OpenClaw skill installation is repository-local unless its explicit `--global` option is used. CLI mutations resolve `--actor`, then `TRACKER_ACTOR`, then `actor.default`, and fail before writing when identity is missing. Supply reasons for mutations; tracked MCP writes and protected or security-sensitive CLI operations require them. Under `review_gate`, required-reviewer approval moves the ticket to `done` without a second completion call. New schedules must be strictly in the future. Treat `canceled` as its own terminal board column: it does not satisfy dependencies or count as Done. Browser archive is `tracker ticket archive` (delete is an alias); there is no restore. Do not scrape the local web board; it is for humans. `tracker uninstall` removes software only. `tracker update` replaces the binary only; re-run `tracker init` in each workspace to refresh managed skills. Atlas does not start coding agents.
